concept.reason: Direct lateral and dorsal same-species fossil photographs, fin tissue closeups, explicit measurements, and a published scientific skeletal reconstruction suffice. No additional generated concept needed; not four real angles of one specimen.

representation: living-reconstruction of whole animal, bounded by same-species real skeletons and preserved fin soft tissue

reference_anchor.context: Sasso Caldo quarry, Besano, northern Italy; uppermost Anisian, Middle Triassic. Nearly adult individuals.
reference_anchor.image_roles: MainFig3 actual fossils; Fig4 actual fin photos plus explanatory drawing; Fig8A published skeletal/body reconstruction, NOT photograph. Fig8B is a comparison shark and must never be copied into animal.
reference_anchor.scientific_scope: An elongate transitional ichthyosaur with small relatively anterior dorsal fin, long tail with modest asymmetric upper lobe and bent vertebral axis; not a Jurassic thunniform fish-shaped ichthyosaur.

scale.basis: SOM table forBES SC1000. Forefin approx/incomplete. MainTable1: dorsal leadingedge and caudal height parenthesized/incomplete. Do not label fin leadingedge as verticalheight.
scale.not_measured: Living axial thickness, fin membrane outline between bones, external eye diameter, exact colour, muscular volume. Working maximum body width0.10–0.14m is conservative reconstruction, not a measured living width. Skullorbit41mm is not a41mm protruding eyeball.
scale.source_discrepancy: Use SOM985mm for nominal total, not an exact length inferred from scale of schematicFig8. The schematic guides proportions and fin location, not a photogrammetric replica.

morphology: Continuous streamlined but elongate trunk, tapered narrow tooth-bearing rostrum with recognizable head/orbit; only a short neck transition. Use skull190mm and preorbital130mm, not a crocodile jaw or a dolphin blunt snout.

Retain long substantial tail and deep caudal body rather than short pinched thunniform peduncle. The small upper tail lobe sits at the caudal peak. FollowFig8A and natural skeletal bend, not a giant symmetric crescent or horizontal cetacean fluke.

Small triangular dorsal fin is relatively anterior, above the trailing base of the forefins/deep anterior trunk, anchored by preserved tissue over dorsal vertebrae15–23. Do not centre it arbitrarily halfway along whole animal. Leadingedge68mm means vertical height is lower; use about45–60mm as inferred outline.

Exactly four limb-derived paddles, paired forefins substantially larger than hindfins. BES SC1000 dimensions approximate130mm front/58mm hind;1001 has132/74mm. Do not average silently or add shark ventral fins.

Fin roots smoothly attached to body; continuous fleshy paddle outline enclosing skeletal digits, no free reptile fingers or exposed bones. Mild lateral/downward spread of paired flippers for countability, not sprawling walking limbs.
Scaleless smooth skin is evidenced. Low-poly facets are style, not polygonal scales or armour. No shell, gills, blowhole, extra dorsal crest, visible gut, fossil cracks or skeleton on surface.
Use one modest eye each side, lateral slit-like nostril near snout base. Closed or nearly closed slender mouth; optional subdued small teeth only if readable without producing a crocodilian grin.
Neutral swimming pose keeps body/tail predominantly straight in dorsal view while retaining anatomical caudal bend in lateral view. No slab, support pedestal, lettering or prey.
uncertainty: Whole living volume and skin colour are inferred. Sourcefossils are compressed; no false claim of measured live3D proportions.
MainFig8A completes soft contour using real fin/tissue constraints. Remaining fin membrane margins and body flesh are interpretive, not wholly preserved in one photo.
SC1000 andSC1001 are separate same-species individuals; keep numerical measurements distinguished.
Restoration corrects documented small postmortem displacement of caudal soft lobe to its anatomical caudal peak, following authors, not arbitrary fin relocation.
palette: Muted slate/grey dorsal surface and slightly lighter underside, artistic only; no unsupported specific pigment pattern.
acceptance_focus: Lateral(front camera-Y): elongated original body, small anterior dorsal fin, long bent asymmetric tail, no generic dolphin outline.
Head-on(side camera+X): bilateral head and exactlytwo fore/two hind paddles, no flattened billboard body.
Top: rostrum slender, continuous symmetrical trunk and proportional pairedpaddles; long tail is not a wide shark fork.
Perspective: all fins visibly attached, modest tail upper lobe, smooth living animal not fossilsurface.
Scale985mm nominal. Skeletal190mm skull and130/58mm limbs constrain ratios. Preparation layout success is not scientificPASS.
